title: Gas Dehydration Unit
model_title: TEG Gas Dehydration Unit (Contactor + Glycol Regeneration)

introduction.definition: A TEG gas dehydration unit removes water vapour from natural gas to prevent hydrates and corrosion. Wet gas rises through the trays of a contactor against a downflow of lean triethylene glycol, which absorbs the water. The rich glycol is flashed, heated and boiled in a reboiler to drive off the water, then cooled and pumped back.
introduction.summary: A TEG gas dehydration unit removes water vapour from natural gas so it does not form hydrates or corrode pipelines. In the contactor, wet gas rises through trays against a downflow of lean triethylene glycol, which absorbs the water. The rich glycol is regenerated by boiling off the water in a reboiler and returned.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Outlet dew point vs lean TEG concentration and circulation rate (typically ~ 15–40 L TEG per kg water removed).

temperature.title: Absorption at high pressure, regeneration at high temperature
temperature.description: In the contactor wet gas (often 30–100 bar) rises through trays while lean triethylene glycol (TEG, typically ~ 98.5–99.9 wt %) absorbs its water. Rich glycol is flashed, heated and boiled in the reboiler at about 200 °C (below TEG decomposition ~ 206 °C) to drive the water off through the still. Typical outlet water content ≈ 7 lb/MMscf (~ 110 mg/Sm³) pipeline specification.

script.narration: This module introduces the Gas Dehydration Unit.
A TEG gas dehydration unit removes water vapour from natural gas to prevent hydrates and corrosion.
Wet gas rises through the trays of a contactor against a downflow of lean triethylene glycol, which absorbs the water.
The rich glycol is flashed, heated and boiled in a reboiler to drive off the water, then cooled and pumped back.
Typical applications include natural gas pipelines and gathering; offshore gas processing; gas storage withdrawal.

script.narration: How the Gas Dehydration Unit works.
Wet gas enters the bottom of the contactor.
Lean glycol flows down across the trays.
Glycol absorbs the water; dry gas leaves the top.
Rich glycol is flashed and preheated.
The reboiler boils off the water; the pump returns lean glycol.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Gas Dehydration Unit — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Gas Dehydration Unit.
Check glycol level, reboiler temperature, dew point.
Glycol analysis (water, pH, contaminants); filter changes.
Inspect fire tube and trays.
Watch for glycol losses: falling level. Common cause: foaming, carry-over, high gas velocity.
Watch for glycol degradation: dark, acidic glycol. Common cause: overheating, oxygen.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
